info.description: The buyer-facing Crossly API — cart, orders, wishlists, offers, cashback. A DIFFERENT principal from the seller API: authenticated by a buyer OAuth token scoped `buyer:*` and resolved by `resolveBuyer`. A seller Personal Access Token will NOT authenticate these endpoints.

savingCents.description: Positive when cheaper. Null when no page price was supplied.

conditionComparable.description:
TRUE means the offer's condition and the page's are comparable. False
means we matched the item but not its state — a used Crossly copy against
a retailer's new one — and the UI must say so rather than claim a saving.

shippingKnown.description:
Always false today. Crossly shipping is computed at checkout from the
buyer's address, which Scout does not have and should not send. Present so
the surface that renders "before shipping" is reading a fact rather than
hard-coding an assumption that stops being true when we add it.

alternates.description:
Other buyable offers for the SAME item, cheapest first, best excluded.

Deliberately not "you might also like". We have no behavioural data to
build that from, and inventing it would put unrelated items under a badge
whose entire value is that it only ever appears when we have the thing the
buyer is actually looking at.

What these ARE is the same product from other sellers, in other
conditions, at other prices — which is the choice a buyer on a product
page genuinely wants, and the one a single "cheapest" result hides.

condition.description:

slug.description:

Present so Scout can buy it without parsing the URL it was given back.
Null on an order-book ask, which is deliberate rather than an omission:
an ask is a price in a book, not a thing with a checkout, and a Buy button
on one would be a promise the market side cannot keep.

Surfaced rather than hidden: "we could not look harder" and "we
looked and found nothing" are different answers, and a client that
cannot tell them apart shows the wrong message on both.

candidates.description:
Retailer products whose PHOTO matches the buyer's, for an object
that showed us no barcode and no tag — which is most objects.

Returned as candidates rather than folded into `identifier`
because a visual match is a resemblance, and `docs/IDENTIFIER-FIRST.md`
permits that only where it is never asserted as an identity. Confirm
one (`hud.confirm`) and re-run the comparison through
`POST /v1/buyer/anywhere` with its identifier to get a price verdict
that is actually about the item in their hand.

What the buyer gets back, in cents, if they buy through us.

Shown because a cashback figure the buyer cannot see is a figure they have

number, because an invented figure is the one thing that turns a helpful
overlay into a liar.

CreateBuyerLockonConfirmResponseCoupon.description:
A code worth trying at the recommended retailer, with the cashback
already on `offsite.buyerCashbackCents`.

`hud.coupon.measured` says whether the saving figure rests on real
outcomes. Render the two differently: an unmeasured code is worth
offering and its saving is not a number we have.

tone.description: `win` earned a saving, `info` found something, `none` found nothing.

imageUrl.description: Image for the lens card, when there is a match worth showing.

url.description: Where a pinch goes. Null for `save` and `confirm`, which navigate nowhere.

identifierNs.description: Where it came from, so a confirmation can be validated.

CreateBuyerLockonConfirmResponseHudConfi.description:
The product a pinch would be confirming, when the action is `confirm`.

Carried separately from the action because the client needs the
IDENTIFIER to act on it — a confirm re-runs the price comparison against
this identifier, and a label would only send it back through text search.
Null for every other action, so a client cannot confirm something we never
offered.

savingLabel.description: "saves about $12" when measured, "code available" when not. Never a lie.

measured.description: True when `savingLabel` rests on real measured outcomes.

CreateBuyerLockonConfirmResponseHudCoupo.description:
A code to try at the retailer, when there is one worth trying.

Separate from the fact chips because it is the one thing on this card the
buyer has to CARRY somewhere — chips are read and forgotten, a code is
copied. Null unless the recommendation is a retailer and a live code
clears the offer's minimum spend.

tone.description: `good` is a saving or a strong signal; `warn` is a reason to hesitate.

Shipping services and prices to a destination.
get.description: Lists every shipping service the seller offers to `country` (default: the seller’s own country) with its price for `quantity` units and its delivery window in business days (handling included). `zip` is required for a domestic quote; `state` is optional. `shipsToCountry: false` means the seller does not ship there (`noShipMessage` says why); `partial: true` means a ZIP or postcode could change the answer. Pass a service `id` as `shippingServiceId` to POST /api/v1/buyer/checkout, or in `shippingServiceBySeller` to POST /api/v1/buyer/cart/quote. A seller on "buyer pays: calculated" prices each allowed carrier service from the live label rate for this parcel plus their handling fee (rates cached 15 minutes): those services carry `carrier` and `carrierService`, and `calculatedAtCheckout: true` means a ZIP is needed first.

get.summary: Is it still buyable, and at what price.

get.summary: Display-only exchange rates (units per 1 USD).
get.description: ECB daily reference rates rebased to US dollars: `rates.EUR = 0.92` means $1 ≈ €0.92. `asOf` is the ECB publication date (null until the first refresh). For showing an approximate price only — every Crossly price and charge is in USD, and the card issuer sets the final exchange rate.

get.summary: Import duties, taxes and fees to a country (landed cost).
get.description: Quotes the import duties, import taxes and fees for this listing shipped to `country` (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), using the cheapest shipping service the seller offers there. `status: included` means checkout charges them now and the parcel ships DDP — no bill at the door; `unavailable` means it ships DDU and `notice` says the carrier or customs may charge on delivery; `none` means the parcel does not cross a border. Amounts are US-dollar cents. Answers 503 with `missingEnv` when landed-cost quoting is not configured on this deployment.

get.summary: Cheapest source for an item — Crossly first, then other retailers.
get.description: Answers with a VERDICT, not a list: crossly_best, offsite_cheaper, offsite_only or no_match. Offsite offers come from licensed affiliate product feeds, are ranked CHEAPEST-FIRST — commission only ever breaks a sub-$1 tie — and only appear when they beat the price you passed in. `shippingUnknown: true` means a compared price omitted postage, so present the result as "before postage" rather than as a delivered total. Crossly wins ties within $1; beyond that the honest answer wins.

Nothing is charged until the PaymentIntent is confirmed; the code is emailed to the recipient once payment clears (at deliverAt, if given) and is never returned here. $10–$500. Cards and their credit expire 5 years after purchase. Idempotency-Key required.

get.summary: Gift card credit on your account, and when it expires.
get.description: One row per gift card you redeemed. `meta.giftCreditCents` is the unspent, unexpired gift credit in your Crossly Bucks balance; `meta.nextExpiresAt` is the soonest date any of it lapses. Spending at checkout uses gift credit first.

post.summary: Redeem a gift card code into your own balance.
post.description: Adds the card’s value to the token owner’s Crossly balance (Crossly Bucks today; CBX granted balance when Crossly issues CBX), spendable at checkout. One redemption per card. The credit keeps the card’s expiry date. Refusals: 404 invalid_code, 409 already_redeemed / not_paid / void / expired.

get.summary: Your saved cards, the default first.
get.description: Brand, last 4, expiry and whether it is your default. The `id` is what checkout and auction bids take as `paymentMethodId`.

put.summary: Make one of your saved cards the default.
put.description: The default is the card express checkout offers first. Only your own saved card: any other id is a 404.

get.summary: Your monitors.

post.summary: Watch a search, and be told when it matches.
post.description: Works immediately — there is no review step. The signing secret is returned ONCE, here; it is never readable again. The first sweep SEEDS without firing: a restock alert created while the item is already in stock has not observed a restock, and a new-listing monitor would otherwise deliver the entire back catalogue.

get.summary: What this monitor has matched.
get.description: The read side of a `poll` monitor, and an audit trail for a `webhook` one — so a missed delivery does not mean lost data.

patch.summary: Pause, resume or rename a monitor.

delete.summary: Delete a monitor.

204.description: No Content — the request succeeded and there is no body.

get.summary: Your shopping agent conversations, newest first.

post.summary: Start a shopping agent conversation.

get.summary: A conversation: its brief and turns, with each turn’s options re-read live.

delete.summary: Delete a conversation.

post.summary: Say something to the agent: what you want, a critique of the options ("cheaper", "more like #2"), or send a photo (imageBase64) to find things like it. Returns its reply and the new numbered options.
Like or dislike an option; the next search leans toward likes and drops dislikes.
Act on an option: save, cart, alert, registry, price (real-sales check), offer (prepare / confirm), or buy (quote — complete with POST /api/v1/buyer/checkout). Needs the action’s own scope too.

get.summary: What this key is allowed to spend.
get.description: Reports the controls for the key making the call — not for your account. Every key has its own switch and its own limits.

put.summary: Switch this key on for spending, and set its limits.
put.description: A key can only ever raise or lower ITS OWN limits, and only if the token already carries buyer:checkout:write. Turning it off takes effect immediately.

post.summary: Buy a listing without being present.
post.description: An Idempotency-Key header is REQUIRED — this endpoint refuses without one, because a retried request would otherwise buy the item twice and a retry is the most likely thing an automated buyer does. Derive the key from what you are buying and reuse it across retries; a fresh random value per attempt satisfies the check and keeps the bug. The item is QUOTED first and the delivered total is checked against both your maxTotalCents and this key's limits before anything is charged. Pass shippingServiceId to choose the shipping speed (default: the cheapest). A card that demands 3-D Secure cannot be charged unattended; that answers 402 with `authentication_required` and the purchase must be finished on Crossly. Optional payInCurrency (e.g. "eur") charges the card in that currency at the rate quoted in this request, including a 3% conversion charge; the response then carries chargeCurrency + chargeAmountMinor. Limits and maxTotalCents stay in USD cents. Pre-orders cannot be paid in another currency (422 currency_unavailable).

post.summary: Identify a physical item and find the cheapest place to buy it.
post.description: Send a barcode identifier OR a photo. A BARCODE establishes identity, so the response carries a full price verdict across Crossly and other retailers. A PHOTO establishes resemblance only: you get visual matches from the Crossly catalogue, and a price verdict ONLY if the matched listing carries a real identifier. When it does not, `comparable` is false and there is no verdict — a price comparison built on a visual guess is a claim about a different product. Most second-hand items have no identifier by nature, so this is expected rather than a failure.

post.summary: Open a Live Shop session.
post.description: Call this when the glasses connect, then pass the returned id as `sessionId` on each scan. Opening a session CLOSES any other live one — a person is in one shop at a time, and two live sessions split a trip across both.

get.summary: Your scanning trips, newest first.

post.summary: Close a Live Shop session.

get.summary: One trip and everything it found.
get.description: Verdicts are returned EXACTLY as they were given at the time, not re-priced. A history screen that silently refreshes old prices shows a saving that was never actually on offer.

post.summary: Identify a held object and return a HUD-ready answer.
post.description: The gesture endpoint for Live Shop. Runs a cost ladder: a decoded BARCODE resolves in ~50ms for nothing; failing that, self-hosted CLIP matches the catalogue; failing that, a vision model names it (the only rung that costs anything, capped per buyer per day). `hud` is pre-formatted for a 600×600 lens — one headline, one subline, up to three fact chips and exactly ONE action, because a pinch cannot choose between buttons. A vision label is WORDS, never an identity: it names the thing so the buyer can search, and never drives a price comparison.

post.summary: Lock on to an object the buyer is holding.
post.description: Open this when on-device tracking acquires an object, then post observations to it as the buyer turns the thing over. The answer improves as evidence arrives — the style code inside a shoe settles what the front of it could not.

post.summary: Add what this frame revealed, and get the current best answer.
post.description: Send only what you LEARNED: a decoded barcode, newly-read OCR text, or a frame when neither settled it. Do not post every frame — tracking and decoding happen on-device for free, and this endpoint is for evidence, not video. Evidence is RANKED (confirmed > barcode > ocr > visual), so a late weak reading can never overwrite a strong early one. When text evidence finds several products, `candidates` comes back for the buyer to pick from — a vision label is words, and only a human confirmation turns it into an identity we will price against.

post.summary: The buyer picked one of the candidates.
post.description: Promotes a text match to a CONFIRMED identity — the strongest evidence in the system, because a person holding the object said yes. Validated against the candidates we actually offered, so it cannot be claimed about an arbitrary product.

post.summary: Answer a seller’s counteroffer — accept, decline, or counter back.
post.description: Only an offer with `awaitingBuyer: true` can be answered. Accepting opens a 48-hour window to pay on Crossly; it charges nothing. A counter must be below the seller’s price (in cents) and becomes a new offer waiting on the seller.

delete.summary: Withdraw an offer you made that the seller has not answered.
delete.description: Only a pending offer can be withdrawn — an accepted price the seller agreed to cannot be taken back here.

post.summary: Retract your bids under eBay’s rules — a typo, a changed listing, or an unreachable seller.
post.description: With 12 hours or more left every bid of yours is withdrawn; inside 12 hours only bids placed in the last hour. Proxy answers your bid triggered are withdrawn with it.

post.summary: Pay for an auction you won whose automatic charge did not go through.
post.description: Returns a Stripe client secret to confirm on the buyer’s device (3-D Secure, a new card). Charges nothing by itself. `paid: true` means there is nothing left to pay.

post.summary: Cancel an order before it ships — refunds it in full.
post.description: Instant while the seller has not bought a label or shipped. Refused with 409 once they have (`details.shopCode`: already_shipped, label_purchased, disputed, already_refunded). Check GET /v1/buyer/orders/{id}/eligibility first.

post.summary: Confirm you received an order.
post.description: Records receipt and opens feedback. It does NOT release the seller’s money sooner or shorten your buyer protection. Closes the item-not-received entry point.

post.summary: Open an item-not-received case.
post.description: Only after the expected delivery window — a 409 carries `details.reason` and `details.opensAt` when it is too early. The seller then has 72 hours to respond. One case per order, ever.

post.summary: Report a seller to Crossly’s trust team.
post.description: A second report while your first is still under review updates that report instead of filing another. `purchaseId` is attached only if it is your order from this seller.

post.summary: Report a store to Crossly’s trust team.
post.description: Files against whoever runs the store. A second report while your first is still under review updates that report instead of filing another. `purchaseId` is attached only if it is your order from this seller.

post.summary: Accept or reject the seller’s partial-refund offer on a case.
post.description: Accepting refunds the offered amount and closes the case. Rejecting hands it back to the seller for 72 hours. To propose your own figure instead, use the counter endpoint.

post.summary: Propose your own refund figure on a case.
post.description: In cents, at most what you paid. The case goes back to the seller for 72 hours.

post.summary: Post a message on a case thread.
Ask Crossly to step in on a case.
post.description: Hands the case to Crossly’s reviewers. Refused once it is closed or already escalated.

post.summary: Withdraw a case you opened.
post.description: Closes it with no refund and lets the order complete normally. Cannot be reopened — one case per order.

patch.summary: Revise feedback you left, within 60 days.
patch.description: Replaces the stars and comment; detailed ratings you omit stay as they were.

post.summary: Move a cart line to saved-for-later.
post.description: Returns the whole saved list. A line from an accepted offer cannot be saved — its price only holds in the cart.

post.summary: Move a saved item back into your cart, at today’s price.
post.description: Refused when the item has sold or delisted. Returns the remaining saved list.

delete.summary: Remove an item from saved-for-later. Returns the remaining list.
Cancel a total request you made.

patch.description: A public list can be opened by anyone holding its share link; making it private again stops that link working.

delete.summary: Delete a wishlist and everything on it.
Take a listing off a wishlist.

post.summary: Share a wishlist — makes it public and returns its link.
post.description: `resetLink: true` issues a new link and kills the old one, for a link that went further than intended. To stop sharing, PATCH the list with isPublic: false.

delete.summary: Remove one listing from your recently viewed.
delete.description: Viewing it again brings it back. Sellers’ view counts are unaffected.

delete.summary: Clear your recently viewed list.

patch.summary: Pause, resume, skip the next delivery, change the interval, or cancel.

Tip the seller on one of your shipped orders, charged to your saved card. One tip per order; $1–$500; checked against this key’s spending controls.

patch.summary: Pause, resume or stop a hunt.

post.summary: Join a group buy: a hold at the starting price, captured at the price the group reaches. Checked against this key’s spending controls; send an Idempotency-Key.
Leave a group buy and release your hold.
Ask Crossly to buy an item back under its buyback guarantee.
Add a listing to a shop-together board.

Your instant offers: live quotes, accepted ones awaiting a label, approved ones (with the prepaid label) and paid ones.

post.summary: Accept Crossly’s instant offer on a collection item. Ops then send a prepaid label; the store credit is paid once the item arrives and checks out.

get.summary: Sets you are collecting — a catalogue brand + model you own at least two pieces of — with owned / total and percent complete, most complete first; and whether you show on set leaderboards.
One set: every piece (owned or missing, with its lowest ask on the market), what completing it would cost now, and the leaderboard of collectors who opted in, with your rank.

get.summary: A graded listing’s cert, checked with the grader: the seller’s claim (grader, grade, cert number), status (verified, mismatch, not_found, or unchecked where the grader has no lookup), population and how many graded higher where the grader publishes them, and the grader’s own cert page.
What you own in the Crossly vault: stored (authenticated, on a shelf), listed for sale, or on its way home — with the price to ship one home.

post.summary: Sell a vault item on the market at your price. It is already authenticated, so when it sells nothing ships in: the buyer keeps it vaulted or it ships straight to them.
Take a vault item off the market; it stays stored.

Ship a vault item home, standard or expedited. The shipping, any storage it owes and the early-withdrawal fee (within 90 days of arriving) are charged to your saved card now, all checked against this key’s spending controls; send an Idempotency-Key.

get.summary: Before you bid or buy: whether the lowest ask is vault stock (keep it vaulted, or pay fastShipCents to rush it), and the grading runs a raw card can go straight to (pass gradeWith on the bid).
Packs you can open: price, every tier with its published odds, what is left in it and its value range, and the expected value of one opening.
Your provably-fair seeds: the active server-seed commitment (sha256), your client seed and nonce, and every retired seed in full so past openings can be re-run.

post.summary: Reveal your current server seed and start a new one (optionally with your own client seed). Refused while an opening is awaiting payment.

get.summary: One pack: tiers and odds, items left, expected value, the chase items still in it.

post.summary: Open a pack. SPENDS MONEY: charges the pack price to your saved card, then pulls one real item by the published odds (provably fair: see /buyer/packs/fairness) into your Crossly vault. confirmAdult must be true. Checked against this key’s spending controls; send an Idempotency-Key.

get.summary: Your pulls: what you got, its value, sell-back status, and the fairness proof for each (the server seed once rotated).

post.summary: Sell a pull straight back for Crossly credit at the pack’s buyback rate, within its window, while it is still in your vault.

get.summary: The price today. When the seller has the same item live on another marketplace for less, this IS that price (`priceMatch` says where from), and `lowestAnywhere` lists the marketplaces it is guaranteed not to be cheaper on. `priceCheck` rates it against real sales of the same catalog item in the same condition over the last 180 days (great / good / fair / high, with the median and middle-half range in cents); null until there are 3+ sales from 2+ sellers.
Price protection on one order: if the item gets cheaper before `until`, the difference is credited to your Bucks automatically. `creditedCents` is what it has paid so far.

Your gift registries.

One of your registries: items with how many are wanted and bought.
